correctness.rationale: An exact all-n leading-prefix identity gives a bounded error of at most 3; dividing by sqrt(n) produces an explicit triangular log-phase profile. Harmonic Weyl equidistribution under Q-independent reciprocal logarithms yields the product uniform phase law; tie boundaries are Haar null. The all-length example uses transcendence of log2/log3 by Gelfond--Schneider and rational-function pole independence. A separate standard-library verifier replayed 45,082 finite comparisons; its finite scope is not substituted for the infinite argument.

The 2023 conjecture with pairwise irrationality is strictly broader; this finding does not claim it. A separately published derived general theorem could still cover this specialization.

originality.rationale: Both primary full texts were inspected: 2022 provides extremal two-base sign changes and proposes long strings of inequalities; 2023 explicitly asks in Question 4.1 about all k-base orderings. Neither establishes the new joint harmonic limit, ordered-chamber density formula, or explicit all-k family. Prior base-2/base-4 race uses dependent logarithms and does not cover these results. Broader classical equidistribution theorems are acknowledged as ingredients; an existing general specialized derivation remains an originality risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed theorem for torus-rotation comparisons of digital palindromic counts could imply all or part of this specialization; theorem and proof portions, not every line of the cited primary full texts, were read.

value.rationale: The motivating papers pose arbitrary k-way palindrome count rankings as an open question. The theorem supplies not just infinitude but an exact, computable positive harmonic density for every strict ranking in explicitly constructed families of arbitrary k; two-base density and equality-zero laws are additional natural invariants. Transcendence ensures the genuinely multidimensional independence needed in all lengths. The value is not predicated on ordinary density or resolving the full conjecture.
